instruments.q: This lamp emits longwave ultraviolet radiation (365 nm) and is used to examine skin fluorescence patterns. Which instrument is shown, and what organism fluoresces coral-red under it?
opts: UVB narrowband unit — Propionibacterium acnes
Dermatoscope — Malassezia furfur (tinea versicolor)
Wood's lamp — Corynebacterium minutissimum (erythrasma)
Slit-lamp — Candida albicans
instruments.exp:
Wood's lamp emits 365 nm UVA; Corynebacterium minutissimum (erythrasma) produces porphyrins that fluoresce coral-red. Tinea capitis (Microsporum) shows blue-green; Pseudomonas shows blue-green; normal skin shows violet-blue.
🏰 Palace: A CORAL REEF glows inside the WOOD CABIN under a BLACK LIGHT — that's Corynebacterium partying in the erythrasma castle at 365 nm.

instruments.q: This handheld optical device uses polarized or non-polarized light with magnification (×10) to visualize subsurface skin structures without skin-surface reflection. What is it used to assess in hair loss patients?
opts: Dermoscope (dermatoscope) — follicular miniaturization and yellow dots in alopecia areata
Reflectance spectrometer — quantifies melanin index
Trichoscope — measures sebum production
Confocal microscope — maps dermal-epidermal junction
instruments.exp:
Dermoscopy (dermatoscopy) allows non-invasive visualization of structures to the papillary dermis. In alopecia areata it shows yellow dots (follicular plugging), black dots (cadaverized hairs), and exclamation mark hairs. Follicular miniaturization (vellus-like hairs) is the hallmark of androgenetic alopecia.
🏰 Palace: A DETECTIVE with a magnifying glass (×10 dermatoscope) finds YELLOW POLKA DOTS on the CASTLE FLOOR — each dot is a plugged follicle in alopecia areata.

instruments.q: This device delivers a controlled stream of liquid nitrogen spray in a focused cone pattern and is the standard cryosurgery instrument in dermatology. What is the optimal freeze-thaw cycle for basal cell carcinoma?
opts: Triple freeze-thaw cycle at −10°C
Single freeze-thaw cycle at −20°C for 5 seconds
Single cycle at −196°C without thaw
Double freeze-thaw cycle with tissue temperature reaching −50°C
instruments.exp:
For BCC, a double freeze-thaw cycle (DFT) reaching −50°C in the tissue is required. Ice crystal formation and osmotic damage occur on freezing; thaw and refreezing with recrystallization produces maximal cytotoxicity. LN2 spray reaches −196°C at the nozzle but tissue thermocouple targets −50°C.
🏰 Palace: The CASTLE GATEHOUSE FREEZES TWICE — once to knock down the BCC guards, once to finish them off — reaching −50°C both times (double freeze-thaw).

instruments.q: The instrument shown is a small metal loop or spoon with a sharp annular blade at the tip used to extract blackheads and milia. What is the correct name, and which acne lesion is it CONTRAINDICATED for?
opts: Comedone extractor (Unna extractor) — contraindicated for closed inflamed pustules/nodules
Curette — contraindicated for open comedones
Microlancet — contraindicated for milia
Steristrip — contraindicated for blackheads
instruments.exp:
The comedone extractor (Unna's extractor) has a central hole that allows gentle pressure to express open comedones (blackheads) and milia. It is contraindicated for inflamed lesions (pustules, nodules) because pressure can rupture the follicular wall, spreading inflammation and causing scarring.
🏰 Palace: UNNAttractive OPEN GATES (open comedones) get squeezed through the CASTLE LOOP — but INFLAMED RED KNIGHTS (pustules) must NOT be pressed or the wall explodes.

instruments.q: This cylindrical cutting instrument creates a full-thickness skin biopsy from epidermis to subcutaneous fat. What sizes (in mm) are recommended for routine diagnostic biopsy versus larger excision?
opts: Shave biopsy — 2 mm for diagnosis, 4 mm for excision
Trephine — 10 mm minimum for diagnosis
Punch biopsy — 3–4 mm for diagnosis, 6–8 mm for complete excision of small lesions
Dermal curette — 5 mm standard for all lesions
instruments.exp:
Punch biopsies range 2–10 mm. A 3–4 mm punch is standard for histological diagnosis; 6 mm is used for complete excision of dermatofibromas or small nevi. Punches >4 mm typically require a simple interrupted suture; ≤3 mm heals by second intention.
🏰 Palace: A CYLINDRICAL CASTLE TOWER punches through all layers — 3–4 mm for a PEEK-A-BOO window (diagnosis), 6–8 mm to EVICT the whole lesion (excision).

instruments.q: This oval or ring-shaped cutting instrument with a handle is used to scrape superficial skin lesions including viral warts, molluscum, and seborrhoeic keratoses. The technique uses which motion?
opts: Comedone extractor — used with direct vertical pressure
Dermal curette — used with a firm scooping/scraping motion at the cleavage plane
Laser handpiece — used with scanning motion
Punch — used with a rotating drilling motion
instruments.exp:
The dermal curette (Fox–Fordyce curette) is used with a firm scooping motion at the natural cleavage plane between the lesion and normal dermis. It is ideal for molluscum contagiosum, viral warts, and seborrhoeic keratoses. For BCC, curettage-electrodesiccation (C&E) combines scraping with electrocautery.
🏰 Palace: A SPOON-SHAPED KNIGHT scoops out MOLLUSKS from the CASTLE MOAT with one firm scoop — that's the curette finding the cleavage plane.

instruments.q: This laser system emits 10,600 nm (mid-infrared) radiation that is absorbed by water in all tissue layers, enabling ablative skin resurfacing. What is its primary chromophore?
opts: Alexandrite laser — melanin
Nd:YAG laser — haemoglobin
KTP laser — oxyhemoglobin
CO2 laser — water (tissue chromophore, not melanin or haemoglobin)
instruments.exp:
The CO2 laser at 10,600 nm is absorbed almost entirely by intracellular and extracellular water, which is the universal tissue chromophore at this wavelength. This allows precise vaporization of thin layers of skin regardless of pigmentation. It is the gold standard for ablative resurfacing, actinic cheilitis, and rhinophyma.
🏰 Palace: CO2 CASTLE is surrounded by a WATER MOAT — every laser shot evaporates the moat (water chromophore, 10,600 nm), not the melanin knights.

instruments.q: This pulsed laser handpiece emits yellow light at 585–595 nm and is the gold standard for treating vascular lesions including port wine stains. What physical principle governs its selectivity?
opts: CO2 laser — targets haemosiderin at 10,600 nm
Nd:YAG — targets water at 1064 nm
Pulsed Dye Laser (PDL) — selective photothermolysis targeting oxyhaemoglobin at 577–595 nm
IPL — targets melanin at 560 nm only
instruments.exp:
PDL at 585–595 nm targets the Soret/Q-band absorption peaks of oxyhaemoglobin (577 nm, 541 nm). Selective photothermolysis requires wavelength matching the chromophore, pulse duration ≤ thermal relaxation time (TRT) of the target (vessel TRT ∝ vessel diameter²), and sufficient fluence. PDL is the gold standard for port wine stains, haemangiomas, and telangiectasias.
🏰 Palace: A PURPLE VAMPIRE (PDL, 595 nm purple light) bites BLOOD VESSELS in the castle corridor — it only feeds on OXYHAEMOGLOBIN and respects the TRT curfew (pulse shorter than vessel cool-down time).

instruments.q: This laser operates at 1064 nm (near-infrared) and has a Q-switched mode used for tattoo removal and a long-pulsed mode for hair removal in dark skin. Why is it preferred over 755 nm alexandrite for Fitzpatrick skin types V–VI?
opts: Nd:YAG 1064 nm — shorter pulse duration required
Nd:YAG 1064 nm — targets water, not melanin
Nd:YAG 1064 nm — stronger melanin absorption than alexandrite
Nd:YAG 1064 nm — deeper penetration, less melanin absorption → safer in dark skin
instruments.exp:
Nd:YAG 1064 nm has lower melanin absorption compared to 755 nm (alexandrite) and 810 nm (diode), making it safer in darker skin types. Its 1064 nm wavelength penetrates deeper (to 5–6 mm) and is less competitive with epidermal melanin, reducing risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. It is preferred for hair removal and vascular lesions in Fitzpatrick IV–VI.
🏰 Palace: The ND:YAG KNIGHT at 1064 nm wears DARK ARMOUR that IGNORES the dark castle walls (epidermal melanin) and goes DEEP into the dungeon (5–6 mm) — safe for dark-skinned patients.

instruments.q: This device emits broad-spectrum light (515–1200 nm) through a series of cut-off filters and is used for photorejuvenation, hair removal, and vascular/pigment lesions. How does it differ fundamentally from a laser?
opts: IPL — uses radiofrequency energy, not light
IPL — emits UV-C radiation for sterilization
IPL — monochromatic and coherent like a laser but with a wider beam
Intense Pulsed Light (IPL) — non-coherent, non-collimated broad-spectrum light; laser is coherent monochromatic
instruments.exp:
IPL (Intense Pulsed Light) is a non-laser phototherapy device emitting broad-spectrum polychromatic light (515–1200 nm). Unlike lasers, it is non-coherent and non-collimated. Filters are used to select specific wavelength bands targeting melanin, haemoglobin, or both. It is used for photorejuvenation, hair reduction, telangiectasias, and lentigines.
🏰 Palace: IPL is a CASTLE SEARCHLIGHT shining ALL COLOURS at once — no single laser beam, just a broad floodlight with colour filters, hitting melanin and vessels together.

instruments.q: This device combines radiofrequency energy with a microneedling array where needles are INSULATED to deliver RF only at the tip, minimizing epidermal heating. What is its primary indication in cosmetology?
opts: Fractional RF microneedling — acne scars, skin laxity, and striae
Simple microneedling — tattoo removal
Laser fractional — hair removal
Electrocautery — wart treatment
instruments.exp:
Fractional radiofrequency microneedling (e.g., Morpheus8, Profound) uses insulated microneedles that deliver RF energy at the dermis/subdermis level while protecting the epidermis. This stimulates collagen and elastin remodelling. Primary indications: acne scars (atrophic), facial laxity, enlarged pores, and striae distensae. Safe in all Fitzpatrick skin types.
🏰 Palace: INSULATED LIGHTNING RODS (RF microneedles) plunge into the CASTLE DUNGEON (dermis) firing electricity only at the tip — the surface (epidermis) stays SAFE while the deep walls are remodelled.

instruments.q: This helmet-shaped device incorporates hundreds of low-level laser (or LED) diodes emitting 650–670 nm red light to stimulate hair follicle activity. What cellular mechanism underlies its action?
opts: LLLT cap — radiofrequency scalp stimulation
LLLT cap — heating follicles to 42°C to stimulate growth
LLLT hair growth cap — photobiomodulation increasing mitochondrial ATP via cytochrome c oxidase
LLLT cap — UV-induced melanocyte proliferation
instruments.exp:
Low-Level Laser/Light Therapy (LLLT) at 650–670 nm uses photobiomodulation: photons are absorbed by cytochrome c oxidase in mitochondria, increasing ATP production and reducing oxidative stress in follicle cells. This shifts follicles from telogen to anagen. FDA-cleared for androgenetic alopecia in both males and females.
🏰 Palace: RED LASER MONKS (650 nm) meditate in the MITOCHONDRIAL MONASTERY — charging up cytochrome c oxidase's ATP batteries to wake sleeping hair follicles from telogen.

instruments.q: This kit containing a syringe with viscous detergent solution and a blunt-tipped cannula is used to treat leg telangiectasias and varicose veins by injecting foam. What is the standard foam preparation ratio (liquid:gas)?
opts: 1 part liquid : 10 parts gas (1:10 ratio)
Foam sclerotherapy — 1 part liquid sclerosant : 4 parts gas (Tessari method, 1:4)
1 part liquid : 1 part gas (1:1 ratio)
2 parts liquid : 1 part gas (2:1 ratio)
instruments.exp:
Foam sclerotherapy (Tessari technique) uses two syringes connected by a three-way tap; the mixture is forced 20 times to create foam at a 1:4 ratio (1 part liquid sclerosant + 4 parts gas, usually CO2/O2 mix or room air). Foam displaces blood from the vessel, maximising sclerosant-endothelial contact. Used for varicose veins and reticular veins.
🏰 Palace: In the FOAM KITCHEN, pour 1 POTION into 4 puffs of CASTLE AIR (Tessari 1:4) — shake 20 times and spray into the spider vein corridor.

instruments.q: This small cylindrical hollow punch (0.7–1.2 mm) is used in hair transplantation to extract individual follicular units from the donor scalp without a linear scar. What is the technique called?
opts: DHI punch — Direct Hair Implantation using a Choi pen
ARTAS punch — Automated Robotic Transplant Absorption System
FUE punch — Follicular Unit Extraction; leaves punctate scars, no linear scar
FUT punch — Follicular Unit Transplantation; creates a linear scar
instruments.exp:
FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction) uses a sharp hollow punch (0.7–1.2 mm) to score around each follicular unit and extract it directly from the donor area. This leaves only small circular scars (<1 mm) that are virtually invisible even with short hair. FUT (strip harvesting) leaves a linear scar. The Choi implanter pen is used in DHI to place grafts simultaneously without pre-made recipient sites.
🏰 Palace: A COOKIE CUTTER (FUE punch, 0.7–1.2 mm) stamps tiny circles in the CASTLE GARDEN — each stamp takes one follicular family unit, leaving only dot-sized marks.

instruments.q: This glass vial contains botulinum toxin type A (onabotulinumtoxinA) and must be reconstituted with preservative-free normal saline before injection. What SNARE protein does it cleave, and what is its duration of action?
opts: Botox (BoNT-B) — cleaves VAMP/synaptobrevin; lasts 12 months
Botox (BoNT-E) — cleaves SNAP-25; lasts 6–12 months
Botox (BoNT-A) — cleaves SNAP-25; effect lasts 3–6 months
Botox (BoNT-C) — cleaves syntaxin; lasts 1 month
instruments.exp:
OnabotulinumtoxinA (Botox) is botulinum toxin type A, which cleaves SNAP-25 (synaptosomal-associated protein 25 kDa) at the NMJ, preventing ACh vesicle fusion and causing flaccid paralysis. Duration is 3–6 months for most cosmetic indications. BoNT-B (Myobloc) cleaves VAMP/synaptobrevin. BoNT-C cleaves both syntaxin and SNAP-25.
🏰 Palace: SNAP-25 is the CASTLE DRAWBRIDGE ROPE — BoNT-A SCISSORS cut the rope (SNAP-25) so ACh supply boats can't dock for 3–6 months, paralysing the glabellar dragons.

instruments.q: This pre-filled syringe contains a cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel used as a soft tissue filler. What enzyme is used to dissolve it in case of vascular occlusion, and what is the recommended dose?
opts: HA filler — collagenase 200 IU to dissolve; inject within 72 hours
HA filler — hyaluronidase (150–1500 IU per area) to reverse; inject immediately for vascular occlusion
HA filler — DNase 100 IU dissolves HA cross-links
HA filler — cannot be reversed; requires surgical extraction
instruments.exp:
Hyaluronic acid fillers are the only reversible class of dermal fillers. Hyaluronidase (bovine or recombinant ovine) degrades HA by hydrolysis. For vascular occlusion, immediate injection of 150–1500 IU (some protocols up to 450 IU/mL) is recommended to restore perfusion and prevent necrosis. Test dose is advised to rule out hyaluronidase allergy.
🏰 Palace: HA FILLER is the CASTLE'S ICE WALL — HYALURONIDASE FIRE BREATH melts it instantly (150–1500 IU) when the vascular gate is blocked by misplaced filler.

instruments.q: This red/blue lamp is used after application of a photosensitiser (5-aminolaevulinic acid or MAL cream) to activate protoporphyrin IX in the skin. What wavelength is optimal for superficial AKs versus deeper BCC?
opts: PDT lamp — UV-A 365 nm activates PpIX optimally for all lesions
PDT lamp — 630–635 nm red light for deeper penetration (BCC/nodular lesions); 417 nm blue for superficial AKs
PDT lamp — 755 nm near-IR for deep lesions; 630 nm for superficial
PDT lamp — 532 nm green light for BCC; 405 nm violet for AKs
instruments.exp:
Photodynamic therapy (PDT) activates PpIX at its Soret band (410 nm, blue) and Q-bands (630–635 nm, red). Blue light (417 nm BLU-U) is absorbed superficially and is preferred for actinic keratoses. Red light (630 nm) penetrates 5–6 mm and is used for superficial/nodular BCC and field cancerisation. MAL-PDT with red light is EMA-approved for BCC and AK.
🏰 Palace: The PDT CASTLE has two LIGHT SWITCHES — BLUE (417 nm) lights only the FOYER (AKs, superficial), RED (630 nm) lights the DUNGEON FLOORS (BCC, 5–6 mm deep).

instruments.q: This applicator with a large suction cup head is placed on the skin to cool subcutaneous fat cells to −11°C without damaging the overlying skin. What is the cellular mechanism of fat cell death?
opts: Radiofrequency fat melting — heats fat to 42°C causing thermal necrosis
Cryolipolysis applicator — selective apoptosis of lipocytes at −11°C (lipids crystallise before water); skin unharmed
Laser lipolysis — photons rupture adipocyte mitochondria
Ultrasound cavitation — mechanical disruption of adipocyte membranes
instruments.exp:
Cryolipolysis (CoolSculpting) exploits the fact that lipids crystallise at higher temperatures than water (~−10 to −11°C vs −0°C for tissue water). At −11°C, adipocyte triglycerides solidify, triggering apoptosis while the overlying skin and dermis are protected. Dead adipocytes are cleared by macrophages over 4–12 weeks, reducing fat layer by 20–25%.
🏰 Palace: FAT SOLDIERS (adipocytes) are marched into the FREEZING DUNGEON at −11°C — their OLIVE OIL (lipids) freezes BEFORE the castle water does, so only fat dies while the skin walls stay warm.

instruments.q: This electric pen with a fine oscillating needle tip creates multiple micro-channels in the skin at a depth of 0.25–2.5 mm, triggering collagen induction therapy. What is the recommended needle depth for periorbital fine lines?
opts: Dermapen — 1.5 mm standard for all facial areas
Dermapen — only 3.0 mm effective for periorbital wrinkles
Dermapen (microneedling pen) — 0.25–0.5 mm for periorbital area (thin skin)
Dermapen — 2.0–2.5 mm for periorbital fine lines
instruments.exp:
Microneedling with a dermapen creates controlled micro-injuries stimulating TGF-β3-driven collagen synthesis. Needle depth is customised by area: 0.25–0.5 mm for delicate periorbital skin, 1.0–1.5 mm for cheeks/forehead, and up to 2.5 mm for acne scars on cheeks. Deeper needling in thin periorbital skin risks bruising and post-inflammatory pigmentation.
🏰 Palace: The CASTLE ARCHER near the EYE WINDOW uses SHORT ARROWS (0.25–0.5 mm) — the periorbital wall is THIN; deep arrows risk breaking through and causing bruising.

instruments.q: This package contains absorbable monofilament sutures coated with small barbed cogs used for non-surgical thread lifting of the face. What material are most threads composed of, and what is the approximate duration of effect?
opts: Nylon threads — non-absorbable, permanent lifting effect
PDO (polydioxanone) threads — absorbed in 6 months; collagen stimulation lasts 12–18 months
PLLA threads — permanent scaffolding with 5-year effect
Silicone sutures — absorbed in 1 month, no collagen effect
instruments.exp:
PDO (polydioxanone) threads are the most common type. They are fully absorbed within ~6 months via hydrolysis. The mechanical lift is immediate; thereafter, the foreign-body response stimulates neocollagenesis that maintains effect for 12–18 months. PLLA (poly-L-lactic acid) and PCL (polycaprolactone) threads last longer (18–24 months).
🏰 Palace: PDO threads are TEMPORARY CASTLE SCAFFOLDING — the bamboo poles (threads) disappear in 6 months but the NEW STONE COLLAGEN WALL they helped build stands for 12–18 months.

instruments.q: This wand-shaped device delivers focused ultrasound energy at 1.5 mm, 3 mm, and 4.5 mm depths to heat the superficial musculoaponeurotic system (SMAS). What tissue temperature is targeted and what thermal effect is produced?
opts: HIFU (Ultherapy) transducer — creates discrete thermal coagulation zones at 65–70°C, triggering collagen contraction and neocollagenesis
RF transducer — heats dermis to 42°C for mild collagen remodelling
Ultrasound imaging probe — maps SMAS without any thermal effect
HIFU transducer — cools SMAS to −5°C causing controlled cryoapoptosis
instruments.exp:
HIFU (High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound, e.g., Ultherapy) creates micro-thermal coagulation zones (MTZs) at precise tissue depths (1.5 mm = dermis, 3 mm = deep dermis, 4.5 mm = SMAS layer) at 65–70°C. This causes immediate collagen contraction and delayed neocollagenesis over 3–6 months. It is the only non-surgical device FDA-cleared to lift brow, chin, and neck.
🏰 Palace: A FOCUSED SOUND GUN fires HOT BULLETS (65–70°C) into the CASTLE'S 3 UNDERGROUND FLOORS (1.5/3/4.5 mm) — each bullet fuses collagen fibres and triggers rebuilding over 3–6 months.

instruments.q: This test system uses small aluminium chambers attached to a hypoallergenic tape placed on the upper back for 48 hours to identify delayed hypersensitivity to contact allergens. What type of immune reaction does it detect?
opts: Finn chambers patch test — detects Type IV (delayed, T-cell mediated) hypersensitivity
Finn chambers — detects Type II (cytotoxic antibody) reactions
Finn chambers — detects Type I (IgE-mediated) immediate hypersensitivity
Finn chambers — detects Type III (immune complex) reactions
instruments.exp:
Patch testing with Finn chambers (Epitest Ltd) identifies contact allergens causing Type IV (delayed-type, T-cell mediated) hypersensitivity — allergic contact dermatitis. Chambers are applied for 48 hours; readings at 48 h and 96 h. A positive reaction shows erythema ± vesicles in the chamber footprint. The European baseline series covers 30 common allergens (nickel, fragrance mix, etc.).
🏰 Palace: FINN CHAMBERS are TINY PRISON CELLS stuck on the castle back for 48 hours — T-CELL GUARDS rush in on day 2 to confront their ENEMY ALLERGEN, causing a RED RIOT (Type IV reaction).

instruments.q: This handheld video camera with a polarised ring light attaches to a computer and is used to examine scalp and hair at ×20–×100 magnification to assess hair shaft defects and follicular density. What is this investigation called?
opts: Phototrichogram — counts hairs in anagen vs telogen only
Scalp biopsy — invasive, shows follicular structure histologically
Dermoscopy of the scalp — only identifies lesional pigment patterns
Trichoscopy (videodermoscopy of the scalp) — assesses follicular units/cm², hair shaft calibre, and perifollicular signs
instruments.exp:
Trichoscopy is videodermoscopy applied to the scalp, typically at ×20–×100. It non-invasively assesses hair shaft diameter variation (heterogeneity >20% = AGA hallmark), follicular unit density, yellow dots (alopecia areata), peripilar white halos (fibrosing alopecia), and 'black dots'/'broken hairs'. It is now preferred over phototrichogram for monitoring treatment response.
🏰 Palace: A VIDEO SPY CAMERA (trichoscope, ×100) peeks through the CASTLE'S HAIR TOWER — spotting YELLOW DOT WINDOWS (AA), thin vs thick COLUMNS (calibre variation, AGA), and broken FLAGPOLES (trichorrhexis).

instruments.q: This laser emits 755 nm wavelength and is considered the gold standard for laser hair removal in Fitzpatrick skin types I–III due to its high melanin selectivity. What is its primary chromophore in hair follicle targeting?
opts: Alexandrite laser — keratin in the hair shaft cortex
Alexandrite laser — water in the follicular shaft
Alexandrite laser — haemoglobin in follicular vasculature
Alexandrite laser (755 nm) — melanin in the bulge/bulb region of the hair follicle
instruments.exp:
The alexandrite laser (755 nm) has very high melanin absorption compared to other hair removal lasers. It targets melanin in the matrix cells of the hair bulb and stem cells in the bulge, thermally destroying the follicle. Long-pulse mode with pulse durations equal to or less than the TRT of the hair follicle (~40–100 ms) achieves selective follicular destruction. Best for skin types I–III.
🏰 Palace: ALEXANDRITE ARCHER (755 nm) fires melanin-seeking arrows deep into the HAIR BULGE CASTLE — only DARK-WALLED follicles get hit, leaving fair-skinned epidermal walls unscathed.

instruments.q: This fine wooden toothpick or sharpened applicator dipped in 100% TCA is used to treat ice pick acne scars by applying acid focally into the scar canal. What is the technique called, and what response indicates correct depth?
opts: TCA CROSS — bleeding indicates that full-thickness penetration was achieved
TCA CROSS — light pink erythema indicates correct papillary dermis depth
TCA CROSS — no visible change is the target endpoint
TCA CROSS (Chemical Reconstruction of Skin Scars) — white frosting of the scar base indicates correct depth (papillary dermis)
instruments.exp:
TCA CROSS (Chemical Reconstruction of Skin Scars) uses 65–100% TCA applied focally inside individual ice-pick or boxcar scars with a sharpened wooden applicator. The endpoint is immediate white frosting within the scar, indicating protein coagulation to the papillary/upper reticular dermis. This stimulates fibroplasia and scar elevation. 3–6 sessions spaced 4–6 weeks apart are typically required.
🏰 Palace: The TCA APPLICANT is a CASTLE CHIMNEY SWEEP — they dip their tiny brush into 100% TCA acid, poke it down the ICE-PICK CHIMNEY (scar), and watch the walls FROST WHITE, like a mini-ice storm sealing the scar canal.

instruments.q: This bottle contains a peeling solution composed of resorcinol 14%, salicylic acid 14%, and lactic acid 14% in an ethanol base. It is a superficial-to-medium peel. What is it called, and what condition is it classically used for?
opts: Modified Kligman's formula — contains hydroquinone 4% for melasma only
Jessner's solution — melasma, acne, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation; produces even superficial exfoliation
Glycolic acid 70% — alpha-hydroxy acid for superficial exfoliation
Phenol peel — deep chemical peel for severe photoaging
instruments.exp:
Jessner's solution (Combes-Jessner) contains equal parts (14%) resorcinol + salicylic acid + lactic acid in ethanol (95%). Resorcinol disrupts hydrogen bonds in keratin; salicylic acid is keratolytic; lactic acid is an AHA providing exfoliation and hydration. It is a reliable superficial peel used for acne vulgaris, melasma, PIH, and actinic damage. It can be layered for medium-depth peeling.
🏰 Palace: JESSNER's CASTLE MIX has THREE GUARDS (resorcinol + SA + LA, each 14%) — they work in EQUAL SHIFTS breaking down the skin's KERATIN GATE for smooth exfoliation of PIH and acne.

instruments.q: This pre-filled syringe contains calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) microspheres suspended in carboxymethylcellulose gel. When used for facial volume restoration, what additional unique property distinguishes it from HA fillers?
opts: CaHA filler (Radiesse) — stimulates de novo collagen production (biostimulator) in addition to immediate volume; not reversible with hyaluronidase
CaHA filler — radioopaque and visible on X-ray with no soft-tissue effect
CaHA filler — biodegradable in 2 weeks with no collagen effect
CaHA filler — reversible with hyaluronidase like HA fillers
instruments.exp:
CaHA (Radiesse) consists of 25–45 µm calcium hydroxylapatite microspheres in a CMC carrier gel. The gel provides immediate volume; as it is absorbed over ~3 months, the CaHA particles stimulate fibroblasts to produce new collagen and elastin (biostimulator effect) lasting 12–18 months. Unlike HA fillers, CaHA cannot be dissolved with hyaluronidase. It is radiopaque and visible on plain X-rays.
🏰 Palace: RADIESSE is a CASTLE WITH A TWIN PURPOSE — first the CEMENT (CMC gel) fills the walls immediately, then tiny CALCIUM BRICKS (CaHA microspheres) stay behind and BUILD NEW COLLAGEN STONE over 12–18 months — and NO HYALURONIDASE KEY can unlock it.

instruments.q: This portable device uses a fine electrode tip to deliver low-voltage high-frequency alternating current to electrocoagulate small vascular lesions, sebaceous hyperplasia, and skin tags. What is it called?
opts: Bipolar forceps — for surgical haemostasis of large vessels only
Hyfrecator (electrocautery / electrofulguration unit) — delivers monopolar high-frequency AC to desiccate or fulgurate superficial lesions
Iontophoresis device — drives ionic drugs transdermally
TENS unit — transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for pain
instruments.exp:
The hyfrecator (from 'high frequency eradicator') delivers monopolar, low-voltage, high-frequency alternating current. In desiccation mode, the electrode touches the lesion to dehydrate and coagulate cells. In fulguration mode, the electrode is held slightly away to produce sparks. Used for telangiectasias, sebaceous hyperplasia, DPN (dermatosis papulosa nigra), and verrucae.
🏰 Palace: The HYFRECATOR is a MAGIC WAND that ZAPS tiny lesions with SPARKS (fulguration) or TOUCH (desiccation) — the HIGH-FREQUENCY WIZARD evaporates spider veins and skin tags in the castle beauty salon.

instruments.q: This Wood's lamp is being used to examine the scalp of a child with scaling and hair loss. Which dermatophyte fluoresces BRIGHT GREEN under Wood's lamp, and which common cause of tinea capitis does NOT fluoresce?
opts: Microsporum canis/audouinii = bright blue-green fluorescence; Trichophyton tonsurans = NO fluorescence (most common in USA/UK)
Trichophyton violaceum = yellow-green; Microsporum gypseum = no fluorescence
Trichophyton schoenleinii = bright green; Trichophyton tonsurans = orange
Epidermophyton floccosum = blue-green; Microsporum canis = no fluorescence
instruments.exp:
Under Wood's lamp, Microsporum canis and M. audouinii produce bright blue-green fluorescence due to pteridine metabolites in infected hairs (ectothrix pattern). Trichophyton tonsurans — the most common cause in USA/UK/Caribbean populations — does NOT fluoresce (endothrix; no pteridines). This is why Wood's lamp is less useful for tinea capitis diagnosis in regions where T. tonsurans predominates.
🏰 Palace: MICROSPORUM is a GREEN GLOWWORM in the castle hair towers (blue-green, ectothrix), while TRICHOPHYTON TONSURANS is the SILENT NIGHT THIEF — hiding INSIDE the hair shaft (endothrix) with NO glow.
